risks: Possible conflict between owner decision D97 and the code: 'endpoints are never launched' against an example endpoint file and a `stub serve` that describe the daemon starting a model server.

Deploying while batches run: several features (D83 pause, control, canary) waited undeployed because a real run was in flight. Run 8 was INVALID after the pause reload until D85. Each hot redeploy risks a mixed basis between batch halves; the D81 halves already differ in server and lane image.

Pause inside a run depends on the SDK (D77), and the current pause unloads the model. Every pause causes a reload, which is accepted only under D85's after_pause rule, so wall time and caching can still differ between paused and unpaused runs.

Vector search is fragile on harder data: the worst-case synthetic set reached only 0.63 recall at 5M, and id-based recall on real chunks tops out at 0.92 because of near-copies. A different corpus such as SWE-bench diffs could fall below T11 without anyone noticing.
Regex search over raw streams takes 8m 46s unless the streaming deltas are skipped (D48). Any query path that forgets the skip will be slow at SWE-bench scale.
Ported code drifts: the guards, tool-call thresholds and switch_to_act_mode are copies keyed to SDK release tags. A new SDK release can change them silently unless thresholds are re-read per tag.

Environment dependencies: the oracle binary needs libatomic1 in the lane base image, bind mounts need absolute host paths, and the zod pin (bug-009) holds 4.100.250 together. A base-image bump could break all tasks.
Provenance gap: run 0166's kill is labelled 'reported' because nothing in the corpus records it. Legacy comparisons that depend on it rest on what was said, not on evidence.
Store tests run only in the link image, so a host `make test` stays green while DuckDB or Lance code is broken.
Public-repo hygiene: the nickname slip had to be fixed in c4d6cd3. Adding blackswan-2 setup files raises the chance of private host names or absolute paths leaking into tracked files.
